title: A foreign listener on the recorder's port reads as a healthy recorder
foundBy: session agent, after make ci failed on a branch and the same failure reproduced on a pristine origin/main

evidence.verified: go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestRecorderPort -count=1: 2 PASS. Proved by mutation: dialling instead of binding, which is the behaviour this replaces, fails the suite. The check then proved itself in the field. A cs-vcr orphaned by a killed run held the port 55 minutes later, and the tier refused in 0.68 seconds naming the port and how to find the holder. The same condition had previously cost 931 seconds and a diagnosis that accused the members.

resolution: The tier refuses to start when another process holds the recorder's port, by binding it rather than dialling it. A dial accepts whatever answers, which is how a foreign listener read as a healthy recorder. The check runs before any machine is booted, and the port itself does not move, because every committed cassette derives its names from it.
details:
The replay tier proceeds against any process listening on the recorder's port, then blames the members when nothing works.

`startVCR` launches `cs-vcr` on `0.0.0.0:8080`, and `waitForVCR` waits for it by dialling `127.0.0.1:8080`. That dial succeeds as soon as anything answers. An unrelated server on the same port therefore reads as a healthy recorder. cs-vcr has already failed to bind, and its error reaches only the proxy log under `.tmp/live-proxy/`.

Every member then sends its model calls to the stranger. Nothing usable comes back, so no turn ever starts. `cs-claude-turn` reports a stalled turn with the interface idle, three times, then restarts the session. Each scenario burns the fifteen minute readback bound. The tier finally reports that the members did not reply.

Measured on a host running an unrelated development server on port 8080. One scenario took 931 seconds to fail and named the members. The proxy log held the whole answer in one line: `listen tcp 0.0.0.0:8080: bind: address already in use`.

The port cannot move. It travels in the profile, the campaign ID is the sha256 of that profile, and every name in every committed cassette derives from it. The collision has to be reported rather than avoided.

The recorder moved onto the host in 110ea18, which is what made a collision possible. It previously ran in a container on the campaign's own fabric, where the port was private to the group.

notes.text: A killed run is one way the port gets held. startVCR registers its stop through `t.Cleanup`. That does not run when the test process is killed rather than failed, so the recorder outlives it and squats the port. Observed 55 minutes after the run that started it. Reaping such an orphan by pid would go further than this check does.
